EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.

Rationale  
• Two dimensions of variation are available:  
 (i) Time – a large, economy-wide credit shock that began in 2008 Q4 and peaked in 2009 Q1.  
 (ii) Cross-section – firms that enter the shock ex ante more likely vs. less likely to be financially constrained (measured directly by the survey and corroborated with balance-sheet proxies).  

• The DID compares the change in real decisions of the “financially constrained” group to the change for the “unconstrained” group from the pre-crisis period to the crisis period. Any pre-existing, time-invariant differences in investment propensities are differenced-out, and common macro forces are absorbed by time fixed effects.  

• An event-study specification using quarterly dummies from 2007 Q1–2010 Q4 will test (and graph) the parallel-trends assumption.  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
  Treat_i = 1 if firm i self-reports “difficulty accessing external capital” (or “financially constrained”) in the 2008 Q4 or 2009 Q1 survey; 0 otherwise. For rigor, “flexible” and “unconstrained” are pooled into the control group; robustness checks drop “flexible.”  

Control group  
  Firms that self-report “unconstrained” (and optionally “flexible”) in the same surveys.  

Treatment timing / event date  
  Post_t = 1 for quarters ≥ 2008 Q4; 0 for quarters ≤ 2008 Q3. The baseline DID uses two periods (pre vs. crisis). An event-study will include quarterly indicators.  

Running variable & cutoff  
  Not applicable (no RDD).  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of the crisis-induced tightening, constrained and unconstrained firms would have followed similar trends in investment, employment, and R&D.  
  Plausibility: We can examine 2007 Q1–2008 Q3 survey waves. No major credit disturbances occurred then; if pre-crisis coefficients are flat and statistically indistinguishable, the assumption is more credible.  

A2. Stable group composition: Firms do not systematically sort into “constrained” status exactly because they foresee larger real cutbacks.  
  Plausibility: Survey question asks about current external-finance conditions, which are largely exogenous to the firm in September 2008. Still, we control for pre-crisis leverage, cash, size, and industry × time effects.  

A3. No simultaneous differential shocks: Other events coinciding with the crisis should not affect constrained firms disproportionately relative to unconstrained firms, except through financing.  
  Plausibility: The crisis was primarily financial. Industry-specific demand shocks (e.g., autos) are captured by industry × time fixed effects.  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Threat 1: Measurement error in self-reported constraints.  
  Mitigation:  
  • Instrument treatment with pre-crisis credit rating absence, debt-maturity wall within 12 months, or low cash (2SLS).  
  • Confirm survey classification with credit-line drawdowns and bond/loan issuance data where available.  

Threat 2: Selection/attrition – the most distressed firms may drop out of the survey or fail.  
  Mitigation:  
  • Compare observable characteristics of stayers vs. leavers.  
  • Weight observations by inverse-probability of remaining in the panel.  
  • Re-run DID on Compustat data (which includes delisted firms).  

Threat 3: Non-parallel pre-trends.  
  Mitigation:  
  • Plot event-study coefficients and test joint significance of leads = 0.  
  • If violation appears, difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD): interact constraint with crisis dummy and firm-specific predicted investment sensitivity (based on 2007 fundamentals).  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
5. R Code Outline (Executable)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast fe estimators
library(modelsummary)  # nice tables
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading
cfo <- fread("cfo_survey_2006_2010.csv")          # survey waves
comp <- fread("compustat_2005_2010.csv")          # accounting
cfo[, firm_id := as.character(firm_id)]

# 2. Merge & cleaning
data <- merge(cfo, comp, by = c("firm_id","fyear"), all.x = TRUE)

# 3. Variable construction
data[, post  := as.integer(quarter >= "2008 Q4")]      # crisis dummy
data[, treat := as.integer(constraint_status == "Constrained")]
data[, capex_growth := planned_capex_change]           # already in %
data[, emp_growth   := planned_employment_change]
data[, rd_growth    := planned_rd_change]

# Controls
data[, log_assets := log(at)]
data[, leverage   := dltt / at]
data[, cash_ratio := che / at]

# 4. Baseline Difference-in-Differences
# (firm FE + quarter FE)
did_capex <- feols(capex_growth ~ treat*post + log_assets + leverage + cash_ratio | 
                   firm_id + quarter, cluster = "firm_id", data = data)
did_emp   <- feols(emp_growth   ~ treat*post + log_assets + leverage + cash_ratio | 
                   firm_id + quarter, cluster = "firm_id", data = data)
did_rd    <- feols(rd_growth    ~ treat*post + log_assets + leverage + cash_ratio | 
                   firm_id + quarter, cluster = "firm_id", data = data)

modelsummary(list(did_capex, did_emp, did_rd),
             stars = TRUE, output = "markdown")

# 5. Event-study (only capex shown)
data[, time_to_crisis := as.integer(quarter_index - which(quarters=="2008 Q4"))]
es_capex <- feols(capex_growth ~ i(time_to_crisis, treat, ref = -1) | 
                  firm_id + quarter, cluster = "firm_id", data = data)
iplot(es_capex) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Event-study: Constrained vs. Unconstrained – CapEx")

# 6. Robustness: IV for 'treat' (rating_absence as instrument)
data[, unrated := as.integer(is.na(splticrm))]
iv_capex <- feols(capex_growth ~ 1 | firm_id + quarter | 
                  (treat ~ unrated) + log_assets + leverage + cash_ratio,
                  cluster = "firm_id", data = data)

modelsummary(list(did_capex, iv_capex),
             gof_omit = 'IC|F', stars = TRUE)
```

----------------------------------------------------------------  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Economic theory (pecking-order, costly external finance) predicts that firms facing tight constraints will slash investment more aggressively when credit dries up. Prior literature (e.g., Campello et al. 2010) finds 10–20 percentage-point larger cuts. I expect:  

• CapEx growth for constrained firms falls ≈ 15 ppt more than for unconstrained.  
• Planned employment: ≈ 7 ppt larger decline.  
• R&D: ≈ 8 ppt larger decline (smaller absolute number but more persistent).  

All coefficients on Treat×Post should be negative and significant at the 1–5 % level.  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
7. Validity Checklist (Self-Assessment)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
(C1–C5 tailored to DID; 1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)  

C1. Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically confirmed …………………. 0.9  
C2. No spillovers between groups (one firm’s constraint doesn’t affect another’s capex) …………………………… 0.8  
C3. Stable unit composition (no systematic attrition bias) ………………… 0.7  
C4. Correct timing of treatment (no anticipation, clear shock date) …… 0.9  
C5. Consistency of treatment definition across time & firms ……………… 0.8  

Overall, while some concerns remain (especially attrition and self-report bias), the DID strategy is likely to deliver credible causal estimates when supplemented with the proposed robustness checks and an IV validation.
